original_question: Solve d-bar in Lp in bounded pseudoconvex domains, without necessarily smooth boundary, 1 < p < 2.
target_in_paper: The relevant target is the paper’s unnumbered open-problem entry in the ∂̄/PDE part of this problem list: whether one can solve ∂̄ in L^p on bounded pseudoconvex domains without assuming smooth boundary, for 1<p<2. This arXiv item is itself a problem list rather than a theorem paper, so there is no Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3 in this item to target. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9509202))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core mathematical content very well: the operator is ∂̄, the functional setting is L^p, the domains are bounded pseudoconvex domains, boundary smoothness is not to be assumed, and the range 1<p<2 is the paper-faithful range singled out by the surrounding Fornæss–Sibony context once p>2 is known to fail. ([mathunion.org](https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1990.2/ICM1990.2.ocr.pdf?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: State the ambient space explicitly: Ω should be a bounded pseudoconvex domain in ℂ^n.
Make the quantifier explicit: the question is about all such bounded pseudoconvex domains Ω, not a special example.
Specify what data are being solved for: typically a ∂̄-closed (0,1)-form f with coefficients in L^p(Ω).
Specify what a solution is: find u in L^p(Ω) such that ∂̄u=f on Ω, at least in the weak/distributional sense.
Say whether an a priori estimate is part of the intended problem: one normally wants a Hörmander-type estimate ||u||_{L^p(Ω)}≤C_{p,Ω}||f||_{L^p(Ω)}.
Clarify that no boundary regularity beyond bounded pseudoconvexity is assumed.
Clarify that the range is the full interval 1<p<2, not just a single p.
Avoid the informal verb 'solve d-bar' unless the datum and target spaces are spelled out.
refined_question: Let Ω⊂⊂ℂ^n be a bounded pseudoconvex domain, with no smoothness assumption on ∂Ω, and let 1<p<2. Is it true that for every ∂̄-closed (0,1)-form f with coefficients in L^p(Ω), there exists u∈L^p(Ω) such that ∂̄u=f on Ω, ideally with an estimate of the form ||u||_{L^p(Ω)}≤C_{p,Ω}||f||_{L^p(Ω)}?
justification: The paper at arXiv:math/9509202 is a collected problem list, so the right target is an unnumbered open problem rather than a numbered conjecture/theorem. The closest paper-faithful sharpening of your draft is not to broaden to smooth domains, finite-type domains, or p>2, because the nearby historical context is precisely that p>2 fails on nonsmooth pseudoconvex domains and even later on some smooth bounded pseudoconvex domains; this makes the surviving paper-faithful open range 1<p<2. The only substantial additions needed to make your draft stand alone are the ambient space ℂ^n, the datum f, the meaning of “solve ∂̄,” and the expected L^p estimate. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9509202))
